slides.title: Workshop 1– grant IAM user K8s API permissions

body.text: Create an IAM user called clo835-user who is authenticated to access the EKS cluster but is only authorized (via RBAC) to list, get, and watch pods and deployments in the rbac-test' namespace.
To achieve this, we'll create an IAM user, map that user to a kubernetes role, then perform kubernetes actions under that user's context.

$ k get configmap aws-auth -o yaml -n kube-system

# Verify the content of clo835_creds.sh you created

lines: Create a role that provides list, get, and watch access for pods and deployments in the rbac-test namespace only.
# Bind the user and the Role together with the RoleBinding resource

slides.title: Add IAM user  to AWS-auth with eksctl

lines: # Editing aws-auth ConfigMap manually is not ideal. We can achieve the same result with eksctl tool
# We will map our clo835-user to cluster-admin role through system:masters  group
# Delete the mapUser section from aws-auth ConfigMap
eksctl create iamidentitymapping --cluster  clo835  --region=us-east-1 --arn arn:aws:iam::<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>:user/clo835-user  --group system:masters --username clo835admins
# Now clo835-user is part of the system:masters group which is Admins group in K8s. Let's check user's permissions.

slides.title: Understanding Kubeconfig – Working withmultiple clusters, users and namespaces

body.text: kubeconfig is the file kubectl reads (by default ~/.kube/config) to decide WHICH cluster to contact, as WHICH user, and in WHICH namespace.
Clusters – each is an API-server address + its CA certificate (the "where").
Users – each holds credentials: a client certificate, token, or auth plugin (the "who").
Contexts – a named bundle of one Cluster + one User + an optional namespace.
kubectl uses the current-context by default; switch environments in one command:  kubectl config use-context <name>  (list them with kubectl config get-contexts).
In the diagram each Context links a User to a Cluster – e.g. Context 1 = User 1 on Cluster 1 (namespace dev), while Contexts 2 and 3 both target Cluster 2.
One file can define many users, clusters, and contexts, and the same user or cluster may be reused by several contexts (here Users 2 and 4 are defined but unused).

figures.desc: kubeconfig flow diagram on a mint-green background: User 1-4 (teal) at top, Context 1/2/3 (blue, namespace:dev/prod) in middle, Cluster 1/Cluster 2 (teal) at bottom, with arrows mapping users<-contexts->clusters.

body.text: HPA is the process of automatically adjusting the number of replicas based on the requested metric
Enabled and controlled by HorizontalPodAutoscaler resource

The HPA controller polls metrics server every 15 seconds and adjusts the number of replicas on the target resource (Deployment, ReplicaSet, Replication-Controller, or StatefulSet) to meet the target metric value
The control loop, step by step (numbers match the diagram):
Query the Metrics Server for each managed pod's current metric (e.g. CPU utilization)
Calculate the replica count needed to bring the metric to (or near) the target value
Update the replica count on the target's Scale sub-resource (Deployment → ReplicaSet)
The ReplicaSet then adds or removes Pods to reach the desired number

figures.desc: HPA control-loop diagram: HPA box + Metrics Server (top, '1. Query for metrics', '2. Calculate the replicas' loop), Deployment/Replica Set box ('3. Update the Replica count'), and POD 1 / POD 2 / POD N in a dashed group ('4. Scale the desired Replicas'). Green/teal on white.

body.text: Obtain metrics of all the pods managed by the scaled resource object.
Calculate the number of pods required to bring the metrics to (or close to) the specified target value.
Update the replicas field of the scaled resource.

figures.desc: TWO diagrams boxed together in the lower band. Left: autoscaling calculation with Pod 1/2/3 CPU%/QPS, target CPU 50% / target QPS 20, math ((60+90+50)/50=Replicas:4, (15+30+12)/20=Replicas:3, Max(4,3)=Replicas:4). Right: 'Horizontal Pod Autoscaler' -> 'Autoscaler adjusts replicas (++ or --)' -> Deployment/ReplicaSet/StatefulSet Scale sub-resource box.
